result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A gives a tight 7-slide plan and puts the recommendation on the opening slide. It links each backup slide to the hard question it answers and adds a fallback if time shrinks further. B's 10-slide list is reasonable but leaves little room for questions in 10 minutes. It also keeps the ask as the final slide, stated only aloud at the start, and its closing tip mixes up deck positions with original slide numbers. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B states the recommendation on the opening slide and keeps the ask on screen during questions. A leaves the ask as its last slide and only suggests stating it out loud at the start. B's 7-slide list fits 10 minutes better than A's 10, and B pairs each backup slide with the question it answers. Both explain the cuts well, though A's fallback tip uses its own slide numbers in a confusing way, and neither says plainly what is lost by cutting.
